rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In بلاغا من الله, من means a message from God rather than completing the verb of conveying, as in براءة من الله.
rows.anchor: من ليست بصلة للتبليغ ، إنما هي بمنزلة من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading فأن له نار جهنم means his recompense is Hellfire, as in the ruling that a fifth belongs to God.
rows.anchor: فجزاؤه أن له نار جهنم كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خالدين is plural by the collective sense of من.
rows.anchor: حملا على معنى الجمع في من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى attaches to their crowding around the Prophet, ending when they see what they were promised.
rows.anchor: على أنهم يتظاهرون عليه بالعداوة ، ويستضعفون أنصاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised event may be Badr and God's victory over them or the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من يوم بدر وإظهار الله له عليهم . أو من يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, حتى attaches to an omitted clause supplied by the context: they persist in belittling the Prophet until the promised event.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف دلت عليه الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the disbelievers ask when the promise comes, they are told it will surely occur and they will learn who is weaker in support and number.
rows.anchor: قال المشركون : متى يكون هذا الموعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event's timing is concealed; the Prophet expected it soon and asks whether it is imminent or set for a later term.
rows.anchor: وأما وقته فما أدري متى يكون ؛ لأن الله لم يبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمد asks whether the event is expected at any moment or deferred to a fixed endpoint, since the Prophet thought it near.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يستقرب الموعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God discloses the unseen only to a messenger specially chosen for prophethood, not to every person otherwise pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: لا يطلع على الغيب إلا المرتضى الذي هو مصطفى للنبوة خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This restriction invalidates saintly miracles because those called saints are not messengers.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال للكرامات ؛ لأن الذين تضاف إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction rejects divination and astrology because their practitioners are far from approval and deeply in disfavor.
rows.anchor: لأن أصحابهما أبعد شيء من الارتضاء وأدخله في السخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angelic guards repel devils and their whispering until revelation is conveyed.
rows.anchor: حفظة من الملائكة يحفظونه من الشياطين يطردونهم عنه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says every prophet had angels guarding him against devils taking an angel's form.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك ما بعث نبي إلا ومعه ملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading of ليعلم is transmitted.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ليعلم ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers convey God's messages intact, guarded against addition and omission; singular agreement changes to plural by meaning.
rows.anchor: كما هي ، محروسة من الزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mention of knowing here is like His statement that He would know those who strive.
rows.anchor: وذكر العلم كذكره في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses the messengers' rulings and laws, overlooking and forgetting none.
rows.anchor: بما عند الرسل من الحكم والشرائع ، لا يفوته منها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God counts every raindrop, grain of sand, leaf, and sea-foam, so He certainly encompasses revelation.
rows.anchor: من القطر والرمل وورق الأشجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عددا is either a circumstantial accusative meaning counted and delimited or a verbal noun meaning enumeration.
rows.anchor: وضبط كل شيء معدودا محصورا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report promises emancipation equal to the number of jinn who believed Muhammad or rejected him to whoever recites Sūrat al-Jinn.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1237 ) ( من قرأ سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Muzzammil is Meccan except verses 10, 11, and 20, has either 19 or 20 verses, and was revealed after al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: مكية ( إلا الآيات 10 و 11 و 20 فمدنية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء links the trumpet blast causally to enduring abuse: the abusers meet its consequence and the Prophet receives the consequence of patience.
rows.anchor: للتسبيب ، كأنه قال : أصبر على أذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء in فذلك marks consequence; إذا is governed by the implied result that the matter becomes hard for disbelievers when the trumpet sounds.
rows.anchor: انتصب إذا بما دل عليه الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes يومئذ a time adverb for يوم عسير, since Resurrection occurs when the trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: فذلك وقت النقر وقوع يوم عسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, يومئذ is indeclinable in nominative position as an appositive to ذلك, with عسير as predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يومئذ مبنيا مرفوع المحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though عسير means hard, غير يسير emphasizes that the day is not easy for disbelievers as it will be for believers.
rows.anchor: ليؤذن بأن لا يكون عليهم كما يكون على المؤمنين يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this is hardship with no prospect of becoming easy, unlike worldly difficulties that may ease.
rows.anchor: لا يرجى أن يرجع يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحيدا may refer to God: leave Me alone with him, for I can exact vengeance on his behalf.
rows.anchor: فأنا أجزيك في الانتقام منه عن كل منتقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it describes God as sole creator, with no partner sharing in the man's creation.
rows.anchor: خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it describes the man as originally alone, without wealth or children, like humanity's first creation.
rows.anchor: خلقته وهو وحيد فريد لا مال له ولا ولد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, nicknamed al-Waḥīd among his people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His title may have arisen after the verse; if earlier, the verse mocks it by turning praise of worldly distinction into blame for being created destitute.
rows.anchor: ولعله لقب بذلك بعد نزول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him wealth and children after creating him alone, yet he repaid the blessing with disbelief, associationism, and mockery of religion.
rows.anchor: فهو تهكم به وبلقبه ، وتغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ممدود means extensive and abundant, or increased by growth, as a river is enlarged by another stream.
rows.anchor: من مد الهر ومد نهره آخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says his wealth included crops, livestock, and trade.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان له الزرع والضرع والتجارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies his wealth as various property between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هو ما كان له بين مكة والطائف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report describes a garden in al-Ṭāʾif whose fruit continued through summer and winter.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان له بستان بالطائف لا ينقطع ثماره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports estimate his wealth at one thousand, four thousand, nine thousand, or one million mithqāls.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان له ألف مثقال

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says his wealth yielded income month after month.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جريج : غلة شهر بشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sons were present in Mecca instead of traveling for work; wealth spared them earning and spared him worry and separation.
rows.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة لا يفارقونه للتصرف في عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were men who attended public gatherings or whose testimony was heard in disputes.
rows.anchor: رجال يشهدون معه المجامع والمحافل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says al-Walīd had ten sons.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : كان له عشرة بنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reports give thirteen sons or seven, naming them; three of the seven, Khālid, Hishām, and ʿUmāra, became Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ثلاثة عشر . وقيل : سبعة كلهم رجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared extensive status and leadership, completing the worldly ideal of wealth and prestige.
rows.anchor: وبسطت له الجاه العريض والرياسة في قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom asking God to sustain someone's support and preparation means wishing increased prestige and honor.
rows.anchor: آدام الله تأييدك وتمهيدك ، يريدون : زيادة الجاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walīd was a leading Quraysh notable, explaining his epithets al-Waḥīd and Rayḥānat Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وكان الوليد من وجهاء قريش وصناديدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase incredulously condemns his greed: after such abundance, he expects still more.
rows.anchor: استبعاد واستنكار لطمعه وحرصه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said he claimed Paradise had been created only for him if Muhammad was truthful.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان يقول : إن كان محمد صادقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes him and cuts off expectation of further gifts.
rows.anchor: ردع له وقطع لرجائه وطمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His hostility to God's signs explains the rebuke: an ungrateful disbeliever does not deserve an increase.
rows.anchor: تعليل للردع على وجه الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says his wealth kept diminishing after this verse until his death.
rows.anchor: ما زال بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله حتى هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صعود is a metaphor for an arduous steep ascent and unbearable punishment.
rows.anchor: سأغشيه عقبة شاقة المصعد : وهو مثل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report describes the condemned climbing a fiery slope; each hand or foot melts when placed and is restored when lifted.
rows.anchor: يكلف أن يصعد عقبة في النار كلما وضع عليها يده ذابت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another prophetic report calls Ṣaʿūd a mountain of fire climbed for seventy years before the climber falls through it forever.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : ( 1249 ) ( الصعود جبل من نار يصعد فيه سبعين خريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His extreme hostility, culminating in calling the Qur'an magic, explains the threat and brought loss after wealth and humiliation after honor.
rows.anchor: لبلوغه بالعناد غايته وأقصاه في تفكيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, كلا rejects his boast that Paradise was made only for him and announces severe punishment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون كلمة الردع متبوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, إنه فكر is an appositive explanation of إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا.
rows.anchor: بدلا من قوله : { إنه كان لاياتنا عنيدا } بيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considered what to say about the Qur'an and prepared his words.
rows.anchor: فكر ماذا يقول في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words may express astonishment that his calculation struck Quraysh's intended target.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره وإصابته فيه المحز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the apparent praise is sarcastic, or quotes Quraysh's repeated taunt to mock their admiration.
rows.anchor: استعظامهم لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom قتله الله ما أشجعه conveys that someone has reached a remarkable level that would make an envious person curse him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قول القائل : قتله الله ما أشجعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walīd first praised the Qur'an's sweetness and grandeur; Abū Jahl drew him back, after which he denied Muhammad was mad, soothsayer, poet, or liar, then called the Qur'an sorcery transmitted from Musaylima and Babylon.
rows.anchor: أن الوليد قال لبني مخزوم : والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He looked at the people, frowned, turned away proudly, and devised the outrageous label.
rows.anchor: لما خطرت بباله الكلمة الشنعاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says he judged what to say, examined it, and frowned when he ran out of ideas.
rows.anchor: لما ضاقت عليه الحيل ولم يدر ما يقول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says he frowned at the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قطب في وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from the truth and arrogantly rejected it before making his accusation.
rows.anchor: عن الحق { واستكبر } عنه فقال ما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم نظر coordinates with فكر وقدر; the curse is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: عطف على { فكر وقدر } والدعاء : اعتراض بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ثم before the curse signals that the second occurrence is stronger than the first.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على أن الكرة الثانية أبلغ من الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second ثم signals a stronger iteration, as in the cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: ألا يا اسلمى ثم اسلمى ثمت اسلمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then between the actions conveys extended reflection and pauses.
rows.anchor: وكأن بين الأفعال المتناسقة تراخ وتباعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء shows he spoke as soon as the phrase occurred to him.
rows.anchor: لم يتمالك أن نطق بها من غير تلبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second accusation is unjoined because it confirms the first.
rows.anchor: من الأولى مجرى التوكيد من المؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سأصليه سقر replaces the earlier promise that he would endure Ṣaʿūd.
rows.anchor: بدل من { سأرهقه صعودا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Saqar destroys everything cast into it, then restores it rather than leaving it dead.
rows.anchor: شيئا يلقى فيها إلا أهلكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it spares nothing and releases nothing from destruction; all thrown there is inevitably destroyed.
rows.anchor: كل ما يطرح فيها هالك لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لواحة derives from scorching heat; a cited poem uses لاحك for scorching, and the fire leaves skin blacker than night.
rows.anchor: لواحة } من لوح الهجير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line witnesses the scorching sense of لاحك and لاحنى.
rows.anchor: تقول ما لاحك يا مسافر … يا آبنة عمي لاحنى الهواجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: البشر means the upper layers of skin.
rows.anchor: والبشر : أعالي الجلود . وعن الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets لواحة as making the fire visible to people, comparing it to seeing Hell with certainty.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن . تلوح للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts لواحة in the accusative as emphatic specification, heightening the threat.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( لواحة ) نصبا على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nineteen are angels who administer Saqar and exercise authority over its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي يلي أمرها ويتسلط على أهلها تسعة عشر ملكا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations take the nineteen to mean a class of angels, a description, or leaders.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صنفا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has a silent ع to avoid successive vowel movements in a compound-like expression.
rows.anchor: بسكون العين لتوالي الحركات في ما هو في حكم اسم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading تسعة أعشر is the plural of عشير, like أيمان as the plural of يمين.
rows.anchor: جمع عشير ، مثل : يمين وأيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels guard the fire because they differ in kind from the punished, lack fellow-feeling, are zealous in God's cause, and are exceptionally strong.
rows.anchor: لأنهم خلاف جنس المعذبين من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: One angel can push more people into Hell with one shove than the tribes of Rabīʿa and Muḍar, according to ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار : واحد منهم يدفع بالدفعة الواحدة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report describes the guardians as lightning-eyed and hook-mouthed, each as strong as the human and jinn races, driving whole nations into the fire beneath mountains.
rows.anchor: كأن أعينهم البرق ، وكأن أفواههم الصياصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jahl mocked the nineteen and challenged Quraysh to overpower them; Abū al-Ashadd volunteered to handle seventeen, and the revelation answered that the guardians are angels, not vulnerable men.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جهل لقريش : ثكلتكم أمهاتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Ashadd ibn Usayd ibn Kalda, described as strong, offered to handle seventeen guardians and asked the others to handle two.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply says guardians are angels rather than men of the disbelievers' kind who can be overpowered.
rows.anchor: أي ما جعلناهم رجالا من جنسكم يطاقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial itself is not the cause of the outcomes; the number nineteen is substituted with a number liable to cause that trial.
rows.anchor: وإنما العدة نفسها هي التي جعلت سببا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of Scripture recognize nineteen from their books and take it as confirmation of the Qur'an's divine origin, while unbelievers mock the number.
rows.anchor: لأن عدتهم تسعة عشر في الكتابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers grow in faith by accepting this as they accepted other revelations and by seeing Scripture readers confirm it.
rows.anchor: لتصديقهم بذلك كما صدقوا سائر ما أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stating certainty and absence of doubt emphasizes believers' composure and contrasts them with doubting hypocrites and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إذا جمع لهم إثبات اليقين ونفي الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hypocrisy arose in Medina, this Meccan verse predicts the hypocrites who would appear there after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: المنافقون الذين ينجمون في مستقبل الزمان بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, disease means doubt: most Meccans doubted, while some were certain the message was false.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالمرض : الشك والارتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal لام need not state an intended goal; it can state a cause, as when one leaves town from fear of evil.
rows.anchor: أفادت اللام معنى العلة والسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثلا is either a specification for هذا or a circumstantial accusative, as in the cited she-camel called a sign.
rows.anchor: تمييز لهذا ، أو حال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the number a parable borrows from unusual speech and conveys astonishment that God chose nineteen rather than twenty, implying a defective number and nondivine origin.
rows.anchor: لأنه مما غرب من الكلام وبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كاف is accusative, and كذلك points back to the account of guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: الكاف في { كذلك } نصب

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَن يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَن يَشَاءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers see God's wise act as wisdom and gain faith; disbelievers deny or doubt it and increase in disbelief and error.
rows.anchor: يفعل فعلا حسنا مبنيا على الحكمة والصواب

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows each host's exact number and its wisdom, as with the counts of creation, calendar divisions, stars, and prescribed acts.
rows.anchor: إلا هو } ولا سبيل لأحد إلى معرفة ذلك

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, only God knows the armies because they are innumerable; nineteen does not limit His power, and the number has hidden wisdom.
rows.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك لفرط كثرتها إلا هو

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this answers Abū Jahl's question about whether Muhammad's Lord has only nineteen helpers, with the intervening clause parenthetical.
rows.anchor: هو جواب لقول أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هي refers either to Saqar and its description as a reminder or to the verses describing it.
rows.anchor: أو ضمير الآيات التي ذكرت فيها

none: The segment contains only the quoted verses and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun به refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الضمير في { به } للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet used to recite along before Gabriel finished, hastening to memorize and fearing he would forget.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا لقن الوحي نازع جبريل القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should listen with heart and ear until Gabriel finishes, then repeat and study the revelation until firm.
rows.anchor: فأمر بأن يستنصت له ملقيا إليه بقلبه وسمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He must not recite while Gabriel reads to seize the revelation hastily and prevent it slipping away.
rows.anchor: لا تحرك لسانك بقراءة الوحي ما دام جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees to collect the Qur'an in the Prophet's heart and establish its recitation on his tongue.
rows.anchor: في صدرك وإثبات قراءته في لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls Gabriel's recitation His own; the Prophet should follow Gabriel rather than prompt him during recitation.
rows.anchor: قرءانه } فكن مقفيا له فيه ولا تراسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will explain unclear meanings; the Prophet may have hurried both to memorize and to ask about meaning.
rows.anchor: كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ والسؤال عن المعنى جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parallels the command not to hurry ahead of the Qur'an before revelation is complete.
rows.anchor: ولا تعجل بالقرءان من قبل إن يقضى إليك وحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the Prophet's habitual haste and urges patience and deliberation.
rows.anchor: ردع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عادة العجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage broadens to humanity's disposition: people love immediate life and neglect the Hereafter because they are created and disposed to rush.
rows.anchor: لأنكم خلقتم من عجل وطبعتم عليه تعجلون في كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses third-person plural يحبون, which the author calls more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالياء وهو أبلغ فإن قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation instruction transitions from the Resurrection discussion to rebuking love of immediate life and neglect of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: منه ، إلى التوبيخ بحب العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الوجه means the whole face, and الناضرة describes the glow of bliss.
rows.anchor: الوجه : عبارة عن الجملة والناضرة من نضرة النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking to the Lord means expecting favor from Him alone, not seeing Him as an object.
rows.anchor: تنظر إلى ربها خاصة لا تنظر إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting إلى ربها expresses exclusivity, as in verses that foreground God as destination, return, or object of reliance.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى تقديم المفعول ، ألا ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since believers see countless things at the gathering, exclusivity cannot mean God is a visible object; the idiom means expecting what someone will do, so believers expect divine favor.
rows.anchor: لو كان منظورا إليه : محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem shows that looking to someone can mean awaiting what that person will do for you.
rows.anchor: وإذا نطرت إليك من ملك … والبحر دونك زدتني نعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Meccan woman begging at midday said her eyes were expectantly turned toward God and the people, illustrating hope for generosity.
rows.anchor: وسمعت سروية مستجدية بمكة وقت الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers expect grace and honor only from their Lord, as in worldly life they feared and hoped in Him alone.
rows.anchor: لا يتوقعون النعمة والكرامة إلا من ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الباسر is severe frowning; الباسل is even more severe, though used for a fiercely grim warrior.
rows.anchor: الشديد العبوس ، والباسل : أشد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تظن means the faces expect a terrible event to befall them.
rows.anchor: تتوقع أن يفعل بها فعل هو في شدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاقرة is a calamity that breaks the back's vertebrae, in contrast to the good expected by radiant faces.
rows.anchor: داهية تقصم فقار الظهر ، كما توقعت الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is the subject: he rejects resurrection and thus the Messenger and Qur'an, as shown by the surrounding questions about restoring the bones and leaving a person aimless.
rows.anchor: يعني الإنسان في قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, فلا صدق ماله means he did not give the alms due from his wealth.
rows.anchor: فلا صدق ماله ، بمعنى : فلا زكاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتمطى means strutting, from تتمطط, to stretch, because a strutter lengthens his steps.
rows.anchor: يتبختر . وأصله يتمطط ، أي : يتمدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it derives from المطا, the back, which the strutter twists.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من المطا وهو الظهر ، لأنه يلويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that when the community walks arrogantly and Persians and Romans serve them, their strength turns against one another.
rows.anchor: إذا مشت أمتى المطيطاء وخدمتهم فارس والروم فقد جعل بأسهم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man disbelieved in the Messenger, turned away, then returned to his people strutting proudly.
rows.anchor: ثم ذهب إلى قومه يتبختر افتخارا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولى لك means woe to you, a prayer that what you dislike should befall you.
rows.anchor: بمعنى ويل لك ، وهو دعاء عليه بأن يليه ما يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known term is the duration God decreed: nine months, less, or more.
rows.anchor: إلى مقدار من الوقت معلوم قد علمه الله وحكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified reading supports the preferred sense of precisely determining the term rather than simply having power over it.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لقراءة من قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferably God determined the term precisely and is excellent at determining; alternatively, He had power over it and is excellent in power.
rows.anchor: فنعم المقدرون له نحن . أو فقدرنا على ذلك
